Fit the initial hazard models

Source: R/fit-initial.R
fit_initial.Rd

Fits the initial (nuisance) hazard model for each event process (Cox models, or HAL), and the baseline treatment model if requested, and expands the data to the grid of all observed event times up to tau. It also builds the discrete product state space of the processes that other processes' hazards depend on. The result is the input to tmle_alpha(), calibrate_alpha() and calibration_curve().

Usage

fit_initial(
  data,
  fit_types,
  tau,
  treatment_model = NULL,
  arms = NULL,
  max_count = 1,
  derived_vars = list(),
  depend_time = list(),
  control = list(),
  hal_control = list(),
  cores = 1,
  verbose = FALSE
)

Arguments

data

A data.frame of observed event history data in long format, with one row per event and columns id, time and delta (the integer code of the process that jumped, with 0 reserved for censoring), plus any baseline covariates used in fit_types.

fit_types

A named list with one entry per event process, named by the process. Each entry is a list with elements:

  • delta: the process's integer code in the delta column of data. Exactly one process must have code 0 (censoring).

  • model: a one-sided formula of the covariates of its hazard model, such as ~ L0 + z. Other processes can be used as covariates by name, in which case their counting process (lagged by one event) is used.

  • fit: "cox" (default) or "hal".

  • at_risk: an optional function of the data returning a logical vector, marking the rows at risk of the process (e.g. function(dt) dt[["z"]] == 0 for a process that can jump at most once).

tau

Positive number. Follow-up horizon; the target parameters are evaluated at tau.

treatment_model

Optional logistic regression model for the baseline treatment, a two-sided formula such as A0 ~ L0. Required when arms is given.

arms

Integer vector of the baseline treatment values (0/1) to prepare interventional hazards and clever weights for. Each value can then be passed as a to tmle_alpha(), calibrate_alpha() and calibration_curve(). Defaults to both values, 0:1, when treatment_model is given.

max_count

Positive integer. Maximum number of jumps tracked per recurrent process in the state space.

derived_vars

Named list of functions of the data, each deriving an additional state variable, named by the list, that can be used in the models of fit_types.

depend_time

Experimental, and may change. Named list of functions making hazards depend on the time of a jump. Each is named by a state variable: a process z that jumps once, or z.k for the kth jump of a recurrent process z. It adds the covariate T.<name>, 0 before that jump and the function applied to the time of the jump after it, which can be used (as a factor) in the models of fit_types.

control

A named list of tuning settings:

  • prune_states (FALSE): if TRUE, prune states not admissible under the at_risk functions of fit_types.

  • use_exponential (FALSE): if TRUE, always transform the hazard increments dH to probabilities 1 - exp(-dH). Otherwise this is only done if some increments exceed 1.

hal_control

A named list of settings for processes fitted with fit = "hal", see Details.

cores

Positive integer. Number of cores used by parallel::mclapply() when predicting hazards across states.

verbose

Logical. If TRUE, print model fits and progress.

Value

An object of class initial_fit, a list with elements:

  • n: the number of individuals.

  • tau, treatment_model and arms: as given (arms with its default filled in).

  • processes: a data.table with one row per process and columns name, delta, type ("terminal", "recurrent" or "one_jump", inferred from the data), model and at_risk (whether an at_risk function was given).

It also contains the internal elements used by tmle_alpha(), among them tmp_long (the expanded data with fitted hazards and clever weights) and depend_matrix (the product state space).

Details

HAL fits are experimental and require a fit.hal() function to be available on the search path. hal_control may contain cut_time (35), cut_one_way (15), cut_tk (3), cut_tk_values (NULL), two_way (NULL), reduce_nk (0.025), sl (a list of HAL library specifications, built from cut_one_way, cut_tk, cut_tk_values and two_way by default), screen_two_way (FALSE), lambda_cvs, event_dependent_cv (FALSE), npenalize_vars (NULL), v_folds (10), seed (NULL), reduce_seed_dependence (FALSE), penalize_time (FALSE) and verbose (FALSE), with defaults in parentheses.

Examples

# Illness-death data: z is an illness that can occur once, death is
# terminal, and delta = 0 is censoring.
head(illness_death)
#>   id      time delta         L0
#> 1  1 1.0836890     1  0.2724785
#> 2  2 0.6539194     1  0.3572619
#> 3  3 0.1212156     1 -0.8616620
#> 4  4 1.1416233     2  0.8083350
#> 5  4 3.6778032     1  0.8083350
#> 6  5 1.0962284     2  0.6127352

fit <- fit_initial(
  illness_death,
  fit_types = list(
    z = list(
      delta = 2,
      model = ~ L0,
      at_risk = function(dt) dt[["z"]] == 0
    ),
    death = list(delta = 1, model = ~ L0 + z),
    censoring = list(delta = 0, model = ~ L0)
  ),
  tau = 1
)
fit
#> Initial fit of 150 individuals up to tau = 1
#> 
#>         name delta     type   model at_risk
#>       <char> <num>   <char>  <char>  <lgcl>
#> 1:         z     2 one_jump     ~L0    TRUE
#> 2:     death     1 terminal ~L0 + z   FALSE
#> 3: censoring     0 terminal     ~L0   FALSE
